issue.title: Example catalog declares status values that do not exist in `example/tracking_orders.sqlite` (`Finish|Payed|Cancel`, `Shipped|Packing|On Road`), leading the agent to wrong filters and wrong statements

steps: The warehouse team is reconciling open order items. Please list every order item that is still open (order_item_status is neither 'Finish' nor 'Canceled'), with order_item_id, order_id and order_item_status, and tell me how many open items are in that list. No chart needed.
expected: The example catalog (common_columns.csv, bi.yaml, sql_example.yaml) must describe the status values that are actually stored in example/tracking_orders.sqlite (order_item_status: Pending | Packed | Shipped | Finish | Canceled; order_status: Pending | Processed | Shipped | Delivered | Returned | Canceled), so that the agent filters with real values and does not make false statements about the data to the user.
defect: The catalog injected into the Text2SQL prompts declares order_item_status in {Finish, Payed, Cancel} and order_status in {Shipped, Packing, On Road}; apart from Finish and Shipped none of these values exist (actual Order_Items: Canceled 3,829 / Finish 3,729 / Packed 3,773 / Pending 3,725 / Shipped 3,671). The agent trusts the catalog: 2/10 runs first executed order_item_status NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') (14,998 rows, counting the 3,829 Canceled items as open) before re-querying; 7/10 hedged the SQL with NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel','Canceled'); run-01 tells the user the data stores 'Canceled' and not 'Cancel' as 'documented' while first reporting 23,727 as the table size (true 18,727); run-02 tells the user that Finish/Payed/Cancel 'do not exist in the data' although Finish has 3,729 rows. 9 of 9 answers spent text on the discrepancy.

fault location.explanation: 'Current status of the order item (Finish|Payed|Cancel)'; PR #58 changes it to Pending | Packed | Shipped | Finish | Canceled.
'Current status of the order (Shipped|Packing|On Road)'; PR #58 changes it to Pending | Processed | Shipped | Delivered | Returned | Canceled.
Glossary lines 'Valid values: "Shipped", "Packing", "On Road"' and 'Valid values: "Finish", "Payed", "Cancel"'; PR #58 aligns both with the database.
WHERE o.order_status = 'pending' (lower-case) matches zero rows in SQLite's case-sensitive comparison; PR #58 changes it to 'Pending'.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zhongyu09/openchatbi/pull/58. The example catalog shipped with the project was written for a different data set than example/tracking_orders.sqlite: common_columns.csv lines 12 and 14 and bi.yaml lines 30 and 32 enumerate status values (Finish|Payed|Cancel, Shipped|Packing|On Road) that the example database does not contain, and sql_example.yaml line 25 uses a lower-case 'pending' literal. These descriptions are injected into the Text2SQL prompts as business knowledge, so the model reasons about non-existent values, sometimes filters on them (NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') leaves Canceled items in the 'open' set) and sometimes reports the mismatch to the user incorrectly. The defect is model-independent (catalog versus data), while the specific wrong statements vary by run. Retained evidence: run-01 = ABB suite_94fd5e30c8ed4cb8ac466f10a70f24d3 (executed NOT IN ('Finish','Cancel') first, then NOT IN ('Finish','Canceled'); answer claims the data uses 'Canceled' not 'Cancel' as documented and reports 23,727 items); run-02 = suite_41fffe5c89b84f02abdf0cae260e1a94 (answer states Finish/Payed/Cancel do not exist in the data). A third run, suite_2c3e92464c554aa9895844383979c9f8, also executed the ('Finish','Cancel') filter first (14,998 rows) and is not retained here because of its size.
